body: Freelancers who get paid faster are significantly more likely to upgrade to a paid plan. The emotional relief of seeing money arrive might be a stronger conversion trigger than any feature we build.

Accountants are holding back referrals because they don't trust that Ledger handles edge cases correctly at tax time. If we could give them a sandbox or a 'review mode' before they recommend us to clients, referral rate would jump.
Users who set up cashflow forecasting in the first week retain at ~2x the rate of those who don't. Forecasting might be our real activation metric, not invoice sending.
The tax anxiety spike in March/April is an acquisition opportunity we're not capitalising on. A lightweight 'tax readiness score' surfaced at the right moment could convert a lot of fence-sitters.
Most freelancers have no mental model for what 'healthy cashflow' looks like. If we gave them a simple benchmark against peers in their industry, they'd engage with the forecasting features far more.

Auto-categorisation errors feel catastrophic to users even when rare. A single miscategorised transaction destroys trust in the whole platform. Reducing error rate from 5% to 1% might matter less than making errors feel recoverable and low-stakes.
